method: A line-restarting glyph chain whose table drifts, fitted on the public practice training pages only. Each line is one string of symbols (its glyphs, a word-space symbol, a line-end symbol at the end); the table records how often each symbol follows the three before it, and a line is written symbol by symbol from the line start until the line-end symbol is drawn. The text is written in 50 stretches of 60 lines. Each stretch uses a table fitted on 8 consecutive public pages, and the window moves forward through the public pages in manuscript order from one stretch to the next, as a scribe working from a changing set of nearby sheets or tables would. No word list is kept from page to page, nothing is copied from earlier on the page, and no rule mentions pages, repetition or any glyph: words recur within a page only because lines laid on the same page were written from the same small table. A line holding a four-word run of the manuscript is redrawn (seed 408, 3,000 lines). On the practice split, with whole lines kept, the share of words of four or more glyphs already written earlier on the page is 0.299 against 0.311 for the manuscript, above the across-pages shuffle. For comparison, the same chain with one table for the whole text gives 0.190 and fails. Limits: small windows make the chain repeat its sources more closely (90% of its words are manuscript word types); this text was not tuned for the other facts and on practice it loses F-001 and F-003, so it is an attack on F-009 only, not a better generator overall.
